html:
The Chanka were a people of the central Andes of Peru, centred on the Andahuailas valley in today's Apurímac, with a hilltop town at Sondor. They had moved there from the Castrovirreyna region, beaten the local Quechua chiefdoms and formed a loose defensive confederation with neighbours such as the Huanca.

Their place in history comes from one war. Around 1438, by Inca tradition, the Chanka marched on Cusco. The old Inca ruler fled, but his son Cusi Yupanqui stayed, defeated the Chanka and took the name Pachacuti. The victory set the small Inca state on its way to becoming the Inca Empire. The Chanka were absorbed, and by 1492 their land lay deep inside the empire. The Kichwa Lamista of the Amazon say their ancestors were Chanka who fled the Inca.
